title: California trip, Lil and Louis, and Joe's new embouchure
summary: The band went to San Francisco and Los Angeles for poor dances, Lil Armstrong met Louis, men left one by one, and Joe tried false teeth and blowing from tongue and teeth before they returned to Chicago and New York.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Then there was nothing. He couldn't get nothing. And then they went, as I say, Red Bank, New York, played around in there. And almost all the men was getting tired. Getting disgusted. So they broke up. Or we went to California. John Cincere came back here. Dutrie, I think he went to California too. But he passed. Yes, he didn't live long. He didn't live long at all. Because he was gassed in the Army. That's what I heard. Yes. And that caused his death, you see. He was a fine musician. And then we went. It comes in time that we went to San Francisco. The band went to San Francisco. Oh yes. Did you go with them all that year? Yes, I went. And Lil Armstrong. That's where Lil met Louis. Lil Armstrong and Louis. That's where they was married. He met her in Los Angeles because Joe had taken the whole band out there. But they played at a five to ten cents dance. They didn't do nothing. It was just a white goose chase everywhere they went. They didn't do anything.
Well that was the one on Market Street in San Francisco. Oh, on Market Street. That's right. I took a picture of that place. It's still there. It's still there, yes. It's a pool hall now, isn't it?
I went there with them. And Lily also, she went and she and Louis made it and of course they remember.

Do you remember, somebody told me that another lady, whom I know, I think she's dead now, Bertha Gonsolin played piano with the band. Do you remember? Bertha Gonsolin. Bertha Gonsolin. She came from here. Her father had been on the railroad, the SP. And somebody told me she played piano part of the time out there. That Lil left or something and came back to Chicago. Do you remember her, Bertha Gonsolin? No, I don't remember Bertha. She probably wasn't with the band long.

Very long, no. She wasn't. Because after they stayed out there, one by one, they each left. And Joe went down, as I said, and his teeth was very bad. He had teeth put in but they were never successful.
He tried false teeth. Oh, he did, yes. I never knew that.

And then he tried a new system. He was telling me about it. That instead of blowing with the pressure, putting it to your lip for the pressure, he blowed from the tongue and the teeth. Oh, yeah. Yes. And he did fine. But of course, all the time he was going to be an old man. And he had so much disappointment all the time he was going back, you see. But he blew very well at a number of years like that.
It's real easy without any pressure.

Yes. That's right. Without any pressure. So after that we came back, we went back to Chicago from California. We went back to Chicago. And then from Chicago, where did we go? Where did we go? Where did we go? In Chicago, where did we go? African. We went back to Chicago and then we went to New York. And that's where we made the free. I had it all backward. That's where he started around, I see.
